business.title: Association between ambient noise and physiologic changes in neonates with single-ventricle physiology after the Norwood procedure
business.description: To characterize ambient noise and acute physiologic changes in neonates after Stage 1 Norwood palliation. We retrospectively analyzed synchronized sound and physiologic data from 12 neonates >36 weeks’ gestation with a Sano or modified Blalock–Taussig–Thomas shunt during the first 48 postoperative hs. Among 1,014,403 audio observations, 25th percentile ambient sound levels were 69.05, 70.35, and 70.75 dBA during postoperative hs 0–12, 12–24, and 24–48, respectively, exceeding published recommendations. Overall, 3936 noisy events were identified. Time in the noisy range increased from 47 min during hs 0–12 to 266 min during hs 24–48. Noisy events were associated with small heart rate increases, somatic near-infrared spectroscopy decreases, and epoch-dependent changes in mean arterial blood pressure. Noisy events were common after Norwood palliation and associated with small physiologic changes consistent with altered systemic perfusion. Prospective studies should evaluate whether noise reduction improves physiologic stability.

science.title: Bioformulations of Entrophospora lutea enriched with biostimulants for growth promotion and control of Rhizoctonia root rot in lupine
science.description: Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungus (AMF) Entrophospora lutea was previously selected as a highly compatible isolate for lupine, and the main objective of the present study was to further improve its performance and practical applicability by developing two E. lutea formulations using peat and vermiculite carriers enriched with various biostimulants. Incorporating biostimulants into AMF formulations can enhance fungal performance and root symbiosis. The first formulation contained proline, ascorbic acid, and hemicellulose, whereas the second contained proline, humic acid, and mannitol. Both formulations improved AMF performance by increasing the number of infective propagules and root colonization rate. Their efficacy against Rhizoctonia root rot in lupine was evaluated in comparison with unamended E. lutea and the fungicide Rizolex under greenhouse and field conditions. Under greenhouse conditions, Formulation 2 increased plant survival to 92% and reduced disease severity to 24.2%, compared with 48% survival and 65.8% disease severity in the infected control. Root colonization reached 78% and 69% for Formulations 1 and 2, respectively, compared with 53% for the unamended E. lutea. These improvements were associated with enhanced plant growth, nodulation, nitrogenous activity, and enhanced antioxidant enzyme activities. Formulation 2 showed a more pronounced effect with increased proline accumulation and caused 82.6% reduction in H2O2 accumulation compared with the infected control. Under field conditions, both formulations improved yield compared with the untreated control across the two growing seasons. No significant differences were observed between the AMF formulations and Rizolex for most evaluated parameters. These findings demonstrate that the developed biostimulants-enriched AMF formulations are effective and environmentally friendly alternatives to chemical fungicides for controlling R. solani root rot in lupine, while improving plant growth and productivity.

science.title: Efficacy of fungicide against cercospora leaf spot (Cercospora sesami) disease of sesame (Sesamum indicum)
science.description: Cercospora leaf spot (CLS) is a major constraint in sesame production due to its polycyclic nature and the pathogen’s tendency to develop resistance to single-site fungicides. This study evaluated the efficacy of Propiconazole, Metalaxyl, Tebuconazole, and Tetramethylthiuram disulfide (TMTD) applied alone and in combination for CLS management. Field experiments were conducted at Metema and Kokit, West Gondar, Ethiopia, during the 2023 and 2024 cropping seasons using RCB design with three replications. Treatments consisted of seed dressing and foliar sprays with an untreated control. A local variety Gondar deyo was planted. Data on disease severity, yield, and yield components were recorded. Combined analysis showed highly significant (P ≤ 0.0001) differences among treatments for disease severity, (AUDPC) and grain yield. combinations, particularly Tebuconazole + TMTD (AUDPC: 905.48%-day; yield: 836.09 kg ha⁻¹) and Metalaxyl + TMTD (AUDPC: 978.00%-day; yield: 793.89 kg ha⁻¹), achieved superior disease suppression and yield improvement. In contrast, single fungicides were less effective (AUDPC > 1390%-day), and the control recorded the highest disease severity (1543.70) and lowest yield (530.46 kg ha⁻¹). Overall, integrating systemic and protectant fungicides, especially Tebuconazole + TMTD, proved most effective for sustainable CLS management.

science.title: A multi-disease classification method for fundus images integrating gated central pixel-difference convolution and semantic knowledge alignment
science.description: Multi-disease classification of fundus images is a critical task in intelligent ophthalmological screening; however, the visual manifestations of different diseases vary substantially, and existing methods still insufficiently exploit local structural variations and disease-specific semantic priors. To address this issue, this paper proposes a multi-disease classification method for fundus images that integrates gated central pixel-difference convolution with semantic knowledge alignment. In the shallow feature extraction stage, the proposed method introduces gated central pixel-difference convolution (gPDC-C), which employs a gating mechanism to fuse central difference responses with intensity responses, thereby enhancing shallow local structural features. In the deep feature extraction stage, a semantic knowledge alignment (SKA) module is designed to incorporate disease-specific semantic priors into visual feature learning, strengthening the consistency between deep visual features and categorical semantic prototypes. On the Eye Diseases Classification (EDC) dataset, SKA-gPDCNet achieves accuracy, sensitivity, F1-score, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and specificity values of 93.73%, 93.62%, 93.64%, 98.99%, and 97.92%, respectively. Under a unified protocol, progressive ablation experiments showed modest mean-level gains over the ResNet34 baseline and supported the complementary contributions of gPDC-C and SKA. After retraining on ODIR, SKA-gPDCNet achieved mean F1-scores of 66.91% and 70.46% and mean sensitivities of 66.67% and 71.82% on the official Off-site and On-site test splits, respectively; however, direct EDC-to-ODIR transfer yielded low absolute performance, indicating substantial domain shift and limited cross-domain transferability.

science.title: Dynamic optimization of encryption parameters in private blockchain networks using computational intelligence
science.description: This study aims to develop and experimentally validate an adaptive encryption system for private blockchain environments using computational intelligence for dynamic parameter optimization. The proposed framework integrates symmetric and asymmetric encryption, PBFT-based consensus, and a regression-based load prediction model that dynamically adjusts key parameters and block characteristics. A mathematical model linking message length, algorithmic complexity, processing time, and verification latency enables quantitative performance evaluation. Experimental results show that the adaptive approach reduces average cryptographic processing time by 59.8%, decreases overall transaction latency by 41.3%, and improves network throughput by 61.6% compared to static configurations while maintaining security constraints. The findings confirm the effectiveness of integrating computational intelligence with blockchain architectures to achieve a balanced trade-off between security and performance. Additional experiments across 4–13 PBFT nodes and a heterogeneous seven-node configuration showed that the adaptive performance advantage persisted, although increasing consensus overhead reduced the relative latency benefit in larger networks.
